record.title: Ras Jedir August 2024 approach-road blockade and passenger reopening
record.scope: Deliberate obstruction of access to the international crossing, with subsequent official outbound suspension
record.crossings: Ras Jedir / Ra’s Judayr and Boukamech / Abu Kamash approach road
record.direction: Two-way passenger obstruction reported; UN annex separately records an official outbound suspension on 26 August.
record.movement: Travellers and vehicles trying to use Ras Jedir; this record bounds the renewed passenger-access obstruction.
record.exceptions: Dhehiba–Wazen provided an alternative route; specific exceptions through the blocked road are not established.
record.imposing_authority: Zuwara-area protesters and armed actors on the Libyan approach; later Libyan law-enforcement transit suspension
record.enforcement: Residents placed an earth barrier on the approach road; Libyan authorities removed it before reported resumption.
record.consequences: Passengers diverted to another crossing; economic estimates for the broader 2024 commercial closure are not assigned to this short episode.
record.relationship: Distinct renewed August passenger episode after NA011 March–July 2024 conflict closure. The longer commercial restriction may overlap NA011 and remains a separate unresolved phase question; do not double-count it. Resolves the August component of the existing unnumbered Ras Jedir August/October 2024 lead.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Protesters reportedly demanded freedom to conduct cross-border trade. No single official rationale explains every phase.
record.context: A fresh blockade followed the July reopening amid armed factions contesting control. Reports distinguish passenger resumption from a commercial restriction continuing beyond August.
record.uncertainty: UN chronology dates blockage to 22 August using an underlying report dated 23 August; contemporary local reporting confirms closure on 23 August, while later duration wording varies. Month precision retained. August 28 is passenger reopening, not commercial normalization.

historical.duration_note: Not eligible for a single continuous-duration calculation; see movement scope, phases and uncertainty. Only August onset and 28 August partial passenger reopening are retained; no continuous numeric duration is inferred.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: August 23 report directly describes deliberate blockade of Ras Jedir approach and two-way passenger obstruction.
August 23 closure observation conflicts with retrospective four-day wording on August 28; month precision retained.
August 28 report describes barriers removed and actual people/vehicle movement resuming.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The trade-access grievance is recorded. Armed-faction context alone is not used to assign a common political motive to every phase. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Residents demanded freedom of cross-border commerce; attributed protest motive.
Specified approach and passenger/vehicle flow; Dhehiba-Wazen alternative. Does not establish restored commercial trade.
Conflicting onset and later official/protester phases prevent uniform continuous interval.

record.rationale_phase_note: One current coded subtype; no assertion that all possible motives have been identified.

rationale_assignments.Phase / overlap: Protester approach blockade; precise overlap with later official suspension not established
rationale_assignments.Coding decision and qualification: Local reporting attributes commercial-access demands to residents; not an official government justification.

followup_reviews.Research finding: The contemporary Thursday-evening wording narrows the passenger approach-blockade onset to 22 August 2024. Actual passenger and vehicle movement resumed on 28 August after obstacle removal. The resulting six-calendar-day difference excludes the separate freight regime and is qualified by the later four-day shorthand and different mechanisms.
followup_reviews.Challenge verdict: Accepted within the root decision; see frozen challenge
followup_reviews.Challenge finding: Challenge packet SHA-256: a839301af38f99f8df3d156829db1cc3fc348226fae7b47d39e4a24e84f740de. Per-question challenge findings remain in that packet.
followup_reviews.Root decision: Accept four new parents/five phases and thirteen native targeted corrections. Keep December/January Ras Jedir campaign phases separate without continuous duration; keep late-2017 Dehiba onset/endpoint unknown and held. Accept explicit 17–18 September NA008 bounds and August22 passenger-blockade onset, retaining conflicting shorthand and freight exclusions. Accept three temporal-display consistency changes with all new coordinates still unlocated. Nine fresh challenge receipts are additional retrieval histories, not independent reporting origins.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions: REC50-R21-Q02 — No exact elapsed hours, universal freight restoration or complete mechanism-by-mechanism history is established. The official UN PDF and one linked Mosaïque endpoint page were inaccessible.

source_duration.Closure or restriction episode: Ras Jedir August 2024 approach-road blockade and passenger reopening
source_duration.Movement / direction / phase: Ordinary passenger/vehicle access to Ras Jedir through the obstructed approach road
source_duration.Evidence basis: The fresh Mosaïque body published on 23 August explicitly dates two-way passenger interruption to Thursday evening, 22 August. Radio Express confirms the blockage on 23 August and describes actual obstacle removal and restored passenger/vehicle passage on 28 August.
source_duration.Qualification: The 28 August account calls the closure four days, inconsistent with the explicit Thursday-evening 22 August onset. The precisely anchored contemporary date is retained, with that shorthand disclosed. Protester obstruction and the later reported official outward suspension are distinct mechanisms; no exact elapsed-hour count is certified. The endpoint concerns passengers and ordinary vehicles, not restored commercial freight. Dhehiba–Wazen was an alternative. The official UN PDF was unavailable in this round.
